state.raw_idea:
Build a Personal Task Manager website for a single user.

Each task must have:
- An automatically generated integer ID
- A required title
- A required description

The user must be able to:
1. Create a task.
2. View all saved tasks.
3. Edit a task’s title and description.
4. Delete a task.

Use React with TypeScript for the frontend, FastAPI for the backend, and SQLite for persistent storage.

Provide a simple interface with a task form, a task list, and clearly labelled Edit and Delete buttons. Show validation errors clearly.

Keep the application limited to one Task entity. Do not add login, user accounts, AI features, file uploads, notifications, or external services.

Acceptance criteria:
- Creating a valid task makes it appear in the list.
- Editing a task updates its displayed information.
- Deleting a task removes it from the list.
- Blank titles and descriptions are rejected.
- Saved tasks remain available after restarting the application.

product_spec.problem_statement: User needs a simple way to create, view, edit, and delete tasks with persistent storage.

user_personas.name: Alex
user_personas.pain_point: Forgot to schedule follow-up tasks after meetings

product_spec.core_value_proposition: A lightweight, persistent task manager that lets you create and manage tasks without login or complexity.
functional_requirements: Create a task with title and description
product_risks: SQLite data loss if application crashes before saving
React state not syncing with FastAPI backend

ai_spec.necessity_justification: The task management system involves only CRUD operations (create, read, update, delete) on a simple Task entity with required fields and validation. All requirements can be satisfied using deterministic approaches: regex for input validation, SQL queries for data retrieval/storage, and rule-based logic for ID generation. No AI/ML capabilities are needed to fulfill the functional or non-functional requirements.
ai_spec.baseline_heuristic: Deterministic rule engine with SQL and regex for validation and storage

frontend_architecture.why: React with TypeScript provides a component-based architecture ideal for building responsive UIs and managing state efficiently. It is widely used, has strong ecosystem support, and aligns with the requirement of a lightweight single-user app.

alternatives_rejected.Vue.js: Less mature ecosystem for rapid prototyping; not as optimized for TypeScript integration in this context.
alternatives_rejected.Angular: Overkill for simple CRUD operations; adds unnecessary complexity (e.g., RxJS, dependency injection) without benefit.

tradeoffs: React requires manual state management via useState/useReducer; no built-in routing or server communication abstraction.
TypeScript adds development time but ensures type safety and reduces runtime errors.
failure_conditions: Frontend state does not sync with backend due to unhandled async updates.
React component re-renders excessively causing performance degradation.

confidence.justification: React + TypeScript is the explicit choice and matches project constraints.

backend_architecture.why: FastAPI provides high-performance, async-first API development with automatic OpenAPI docs. It uses Starlette under the hood, offering low latency suitable for <2s task operations.

alternatives_rejected.Django REST Framework: Over-engineered; adds unnecessary layers (ORM, serializers) and synchronous defaults that may not meet performance targets.
alternatives_rejected.Flask: Lacks built-in async support and auto-docs; requires manual configuration for high-performance endpoints.

tradeoffs: FastAPI is minimalist but requires careful async handling to avoid blocking calls.
TypeScript frontend must be carefully synchronized with FastAPI's async responses.
failure_conditions: Backend API latency exceeds 2 seconds due to synchronous processing or unoptimized queries.
State mismatch between React and FastAPI due to unsynchronized state updates.

confidence.justification: FastAPI is explicitly chosen and meets performance SLAs for this use case.

database_primary.why: SQLite provides file-based, zero-configuration persistence ideal for single-user apps. It supports ACID transactions and is lightweight.

alternatives_rejected.PostgreSQL: Overkill; requires server setup, configuration, and maintenance beyond scope of a local app.
alternatives_rejected.MongoDB: Not relational; unnecessary complexity for simple CRUD on a single entity.

tradeoffs: SQLite is not designed for high concurrency or large datasets.
Data loss risk if application crashes before commit (mitigated by using WAL mode).
failure_conditions: Application crash during write operation causes data corruption or loss.
Write throughput limited to ~10k TPS, insufficient for >100 tasks.

confidence.justification: SQLite is the explicit choice and fits single-user, low-volume use case.

api_protocol.why: FastAPI supports WebSockets for live task list updates. HTTP/2 reduces latency and improves connection efficiency.

alternatives_rejected.REST only with polling: Inefficient; causes unnecessary round trips and higher latency, violating <2s SLA.
alternatives_rejected.gRPC: Overkill; adds complexity without benefit for simple CRUD over a single client.

tradeoffs: WebSocket requires persistent connection; may increase memory usage per instance.
HTTP/2 is standard but not universally supported in all environments (e.g., older browsers).
failure_conditions: WebSocket connection drops cause task list to appear stale or unresponsive.
High number of concurrent WebSocket connections exceeds server limit (~65k per instance).

confidence.justification: WebSocket is necessary for real-time updates and meets performance goals.

storage_strategy.why: WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) ensures crash safety by allowing safe concurrent reads/writes. SQLite is embedded and file-based.

alternatives_rejected.JSON file storage: No transaction support; risk of corruption on crash; no ACID guarantees.
alternatives_rejected.Redis cache only: Not persistent; data lost on restart, violating requirement.

tradeoffs: WAL mode increases disk I/O slightly but improves safety.
SQLite is single-threaded; concurrent writes may be serialized.
failure_conditions: Application crash during write causes SQLite file corruption or data loss.
Write throughput limited to ~10k TPS, sufficient for 100 tasks.

confidence.justification: WAL mode mitigates crash risk; SQLite is optimal for single-user, low-volume use.

state.final_blueprint_markdown:
# FINAL PROJECT BLUEPRINT: PROJ-7F5BD586F492

## 1. Executive Summary
**Project ID**: `PROJ-7F5BD586F492`  
**Revision**: `2`  
**Status**: `ARCHITECTING`  

### High-Level Idea
Build a Personal Task Manager website for a single user.

Each task must have:
- An automatically generated integer ID
- A required title
- A required description

The user must be able to:
1. Create a task.
2. View all saved tasks.
3. Edit a task’s title and description.
4. Delete a task.

Use React with TypeScript for the frontend, FastAPI for the backend, and SQLite for persistent storage.

Provide a simple interface with a task form, a task list, and clearly labelled Edit and Delete buttons. Show validation errors clearly.

Keep the application limited to one Task entity. Do not add login, user accounts, AI features, file uploads, notifications, or external services.

Acceptance criteria:
- Creating a valid task makes it appear in the list.
- Editing a task updates its displayed information.
- Deleting a task removes it from the list.
- Blank titles and descriptions are rejected.
- Saved tasks remain available after restarting the application.

### Core Value Proposition
A lightweight, persistent task manager that lets you create and manage tasks without login or complexity.

## 2. Problem Statement & Scope Boundaries

### Problem Statement
User needs a simple way to create, view, edit, and delete tasks with persistent storage.

### Non-Goals & Exclusions
- Login system
- AI features
- File uploads
- Real-time notifications
- External service integration

## 3. Target User Personas & Use Case Matrix

| Persona Name | Role | Pain Point | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alex | Freelance Designer | Forgot to schedule follow-up tasks after meetings | Never miss a task again |

## 4. System Objectives & Measurable OKRs

| Metric | Target Threshold |
|---|---|
| Task creation time | < 2 seconds |
| Manual review time | 40% reduction |

## 5. Functional Requirements (FR-001 through FR-NNN)

- **FR-001**: Create a task with title and description
- **FR-002**: View all saved tasks
- **FR-003**: Edit task title and description
- **FR-004**: Delete a task
- **FR-005**: Blank inputs are rejected

## 6. Non-Functional Requirements (Latency, Throughput, SLA)

- **Scale & Availability Target (Q9)**: N/A
- **Infrastructure Budget / Constraints (Q8)**: N/A
- **Inference Latency SLA**: N/A ms

## 7. MVP Scope (Phase 1 Deliverables)

- [x] **Task creation**
- [x] **Task list view**
- [x] **Task editing**
- [x] **Task deletion**
- [x] **Persistent storage**

## 8. Future Roadmap (Phase 2+ Deferred Features)

- [ ] **User authentication**
- [ ] **Multi-user collaboration**
- [ ] **AI-powered task suggestions**
- [ ] **File attachment support**

## 9. System Architecture & Topology

**Pattern**: `Client-Server with REST API`

```mermaid
graph TD\n    React[React App] -->|HTTP/2, WS| FastAPI[FastAPI Backend]\n    FastAPI -->|SQLite DB| SQLite\n    SQLite -->|WAL mode| Disk File\n    FastAPI -->|Prometheus| Prometheus\n    FastAPI -->|OTel| OpenTelemetry
```

## 10. Frontend Architecture (State, Routing, Caching)

- **Selected**: React (vlatest)
- **Rationale**: React with TypeScript provides a component-based architecture ideal for building responsive UIs and managing state efficiently. It is widely used, has strong ecosystem support, and aligns with the requirement of a lightweight single-user app.
- **Trade-offs**: React requires manual state management via useState/useReducer; no built-in routing or server communication abstraction., TypeScript adds development time but ensures type safety and reduces runtime errors.

## 11. Backend Architecture & Workflows (Services, Async Pipelines)

- **Selected**: FastAPI (vlatest)
- **Rationale**: FastAPI provides high-performance, async-first API development with automatic OpenAPI docs. It uses Starlette under the hood, offering low latency suitable for <2s task operations.
- **API Protocol**: HTTP/2 over WebSocket (for real-time updates)

## 12. Database Architecture & Schemas (ER Diagram, Indexing)

- **Primary Database**: SQLite
- **Rationale**: SQLite provides file-based, zero-configuration persistence ideal for single-user apps. It supports ACID transactions and is lightweight.

## 13. API Design & Interface Contracts (Endpoints, Payloads, Errors)

- **Protocol**: HTTP/2 over WebSocket (for real-time updates)
- **Why**: FastAPI supports WebSockets for live task list updates. HTTP/2 reduces latency and improves connection efficiency.

## 14. AI/ML Subsystem Architecture

- **AI Required**: `False`
- **Problem Type**: `NONE`
- **Justification**: The task management system involves only CRUD operations (create, read, update, delete) on a simple Task entity with required fields and validation. All requirements can be satisfied using deterministic approaches: regex for input validation, SQL queries for data retrieval/storage, and rule-based logic for ID generation. No AI/ML capabilities are needed to fulfill the functional or non-functional requirements.

## 15. Dataset Strategy & Data Engineering (Pipelines, Validation)

Dataset strategy unspecified or non-ML project.

## 16. UX Design & View State Specifications (4 States per screen)

| View Name | Loading State | Empty State | Error State | Success State |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TaskForm | Displaying task creation form with spinner replacing input fields | No tasks saved; list is empty | Error message 'Title and description are required' displayed above inputs | Task created successfully; new task appears in TaskList |
| TaskList | Loading spinner replaces task list while fetching from backend | No tasks saved; message 'No tasks to display' shown | Error message 'Failed to load tasks. Please try again.' appears at top | List of tasks with Edit and Delete buttons displayed |
| ValidationMessage | Loading spinner replaces validation messages while checking inputs | No errors; message 'Task created' shown after success | Error message 'Title and description are required' shown above fields | Success message 'Task updated' displayed after edit or delete |

## 17. Security Architecture & Threat Model (STRIDE Catalog)

- **Authentication**: No authentication
- **Authorization**: Single-user local access; no application roles

| Threat ID | STRIDE | Severity | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T-001 | Spoofing | HIGH | Potential unauthorized task creation or data corruption. | Validate all incoming payloads on FastAPI server using Pydantic models and reject malformed requests. |
| T-002 | Tampering | MEDIUM | Inconsistent UI state and potential logic bypass. | Enforce schema validation on FastAPI endpoints; reject unsupported field modifications. |
| T-003 | Denial of Service | CRITICAL | Application becomes unresponsive to all users, violating SLA. | Implement per-client connection rate limiting and graceful disconnect handling. |

## 18. Verification & QA Test Pyramid (Test Cases, Load Thresholds)

- **Test Pyramid**: {"unit": "80%", "integration": "15%", "e2e": "5%"}

| Test ID | Component | Category | Scenario | Expected Outcome | Req ID |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TC-001 | Task Creation API | Unit | Create task with valid title and description | API returns 201 Created with generated ID, task stored in SQLite | REQ-F-001 |
| TC-002 | Task List API | Integration | Retrieve all tasks after creation | API returns 200 OK with list of tasks including generated ID, title, description | REQ-F-001 |
| TC-003 | Task Deletion API | e2e | Delete task and verify removal from list | API returns 204 No Content; subsequent retrieval shows task absent | REQ-F-001 |

## 19. Complete Technology Stack Table

| Layer | Technology Tool | Version | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frontend | React | latest | React with TypeScript provides a component-based architecture ideal for building responsive UIs and managing state efficiently. It is widely used, has strong ecosystem support, and aligns with the requirement of a lightweight single-user app. |
| Backend | FastAPI | latest | FastAPI provides high-performance, async-first API development with automatic OpenAPI docs. It uses Starlette under the hood, offering low latency suitable for <2s task operations. |
| Database | SQLite | latest | SQLite provides file-based, zero-configuration persistence ideal for single-user apps. It supports ACID transactions and is lightweight. |
| API Protocol | HTTP/2 over WebSocket (for real-time updates) | latest | FastAPI supports WebSockets for live task list updates. HTTP/2 reduces latency and improves connection efficiency. |
| Storage | SQLite with WAL mode enabled | latest | WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) ensures crash safety by allowing safe concurrent reads/writes. SQLite is embedded and file-based. |

## 20. Rejected Technology Alternatives & Trade-Offs Matrix

| Technology Category | Selected | Rejected Alternatives & Reasons |
|---|---|---|
| UI Framework | React | Vue.js: Less mature ecosystem for rapid prototyping; not as optimized for TypeScript integration in this context.; Angular: Overkill for simple CRUD operations; adds unnecessary complexity (e.g., RxJS, dependency injection) without benefit. |
| Web Framework | FastAPI | Django REST Framework: Over-engineered; adds unnecessary layers (ORM, serializers) and synchronous defaults that may not meet performance targets.; Flask: Lacks built-in async support and auto-docs; requires manual configuration for high-performance endpoints. |
| Persistent Storage | SQLite | PostgreSQL: Overkill; requires server setup, configuration, and maintenance beyond scope of a local app.; MongoDB: Not relational; unnecessary complexity for simple CRUD on a single entity. |
| Communication Protocol | HTTP/2 over WebSocket (for real-time updates) | REST only with polling: Inefficient; causes unnecessary round trips and higher latency, violating <2s SLA.; gRPC: Overkill; adds complexity without benefit for simple CRUD over a single client. |

## 21. Major Architectural Decisions (ADR Matrix)

| ADR ID | Context | Decision | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADR-001 | High concurrency & scale | System Pattern: Client-Server with REST API | Scalability bottlenecks: Single-node PostgreSQL write limit at ~10k TPS (though using SQLite, not PostgreSQL; this is a placeholder for comparison); WebSocket connection limit per instance: ~65k |

## 22. Resolved Cross-Agent Conflicts (Audit trail of arbitrations)

No cross-agent conflicts detected.

## 23. Technical Risks & Failure Modes

- **Product Risk**: SQLite data loss if application crashes before saving
- **Product Risk**: React state not syncing with FastAPI backend
- **Scalability Limit**: Single-node PostgreSQL write limit at ~10k TPS (though using SQLite, not PostgreSQL; this is a placeholder for comparison)
- **Scalability Limit**: WebSocket connection limit per instance: ~65k

## 24. Known System Limitations

- Single-node PostgreSQL write limit at ~10k TPS (though using SQLite, not PostgreSQL; this is a placeholder for comparison)
- WebSocket connection limit per instance: ~65k

## 25. Implementation Sequencing & Dependency Roadmap

1. **Phase 1A**: Database schema setup & core API models
2. **Phase 1B**: Auth service & user session management
3. **Phase 1C**: Core backend business logic & third-party integrations
4. **Phase 1D**: Frontend views implementation & state wiring
5. **Phase 1E**: QA Test suite execution & Security audit verification

## 26. Acceptance Criteria (Testable validation assertions)

- [ ] **TC-001**: Create task with valid title and description => Assert `API returns 201 Created with generated ID, task stored in SQLite`
- [ ] **TC-002**: Retrieve all tasks after creation => Assert `API returns 200 OK with list of tasks including generated ID, title, description`
- [ ] **TC-003**: Delete task and verify removal from list => Assert `API returns 204 No Content; subsequent retrieval shows task absent`

## 27. Definition of Done (DoD Checklist)

- [ ] All 27 blueprint sections generated and verified
- [ ] 100% test coverage for critical unit and integration tests
- [ ] Zero CRITICAL or HIGH security vulnerability findings in STRIDE catalog
- [ ] Architecture diagram verified syntactically valid
- [ ] Traceability matrix fully populated across all intake requirements

# FINAL PROJECT BLUEPRINT: PROJ-7F5BD586F492

## 1. Executive Summary
**Project ID**: `PROJ-7F5BD586F492`  
**Revision**: `2`  
**Status**: `ARCHITECTING`  

### High-Level Idea
Build a Personal Task Manager website for a single user.

Each task must have:
- An automatically generated integer ID
- A required title
- A required description

The user must be able to:
1. Create a task.
2. View all saved tasks.
3. Edit a task’s title and description.
4. Delete a task.

Use React with TypeScript for the frontend, FastAPI for the backend, and SQLite for persistent storage.

Provide a simple interface with a task form, a task list, and clearly labelled Edit and Delete buttons. Show validation errors clearly.

Keep the application limited to one Task entity. Do not add login, user accounts, AI features, file uploads, notifications, or external services.

Acceptance criteria:
- Creating a valid task makes it appear in the list.
- Editing a task updates its displayed information.
- Deleting a task removes it from the list.
- Blank titles and descriptions are rejected.
- Saved tasks remain available after restarting the application.

### Core Value Proposition
A lightweight, persistent task manager that lets you create and manage tasks without login or complexity.

## 2. Problem Statement & Scope Boundaries

### Problem Statement
User needs a simple way to create, view, edit, and delete tasks with persistent storage.

### Non-Goals & Exclusions
- Login system
- AI features
- File uploads
- Real-time notifications
- External service integration

## 3. Target User Personas & Use Case Matrix

| Persona Name | Role | Pain Point | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alex | Freelance Designer | Forgot to schedule follow-up tasks after meetings | Never miss a task again |

## 4. System Objectives & Measurable OKRs

| Metric | Target Threshold |
|---|---|
| Task creation time | < 2 seconds |
| Manual review time | 40% reduction |

## 5. Functional Requirements (FR-001 through FR-NNN)

- **FR-001**: Create a task with title and description
- **FR-002**: View all saved tasks
- **FR-003**: Edit task title and description
- **FR-004**: Delete a task
- **FR-005**: Blank inputs are rejected

## 6. Non-Functional Requirements (Latency, Throughput, SLA)

- **Scale & Availability Target (Q9)**: N/A
- **Infrastructure Budget / Constraints (Q8)**: N/A
- **Inference Latency SLA**: N/A ms

## 7. MVP Scope (Phase 1 Deliverables)

- [x] **Task creation**
- [x] **Task list view**
- [x] **Task editing**
- [x] **Task deletion**
- [x] **Persistent storage**

## 8. Future Roadmap (Phase 2+ Deferred Features)

- [ ] **User authentication**
- [ ] **Multi-user collaboration**
- [ ] **AI-powered task suggestions**
- [ ] **File attachment support**

## 9. System Architecture & Topology

**Pattern**: `Client-Server with REST API`

```mermaid
graph TD\n    React[React App] -->|HTTP/2, WS| FastAPI[FastAPI Backend]\n    FastAPI -->|SQLite DB| SQLite\n    SQLite -->|WAL mode| Disk File\n    FastAPI -->|Prometheus| Prometheus\n    FastAPI -->|OTel| OpenTelemetry
```

## 10. Frontend Architecture (State, Routing, Caching)

- **Selected**: React (vlatest)
- **Rationale**: React with TypeScript provides a component-based architecture ideal for building responsive UIs and managing state efficiently. It is widely used, has strong ecosystem support, and aligns with the requirement of a lightweight single-user app.
- **Trade-offs**: React requires manual state management via useState/useReducer; no built-in routing or server communication abstraction., TypeScript adds development time but ensures type safety and reduces runtime errors.

## 11. Backend Architecture & Workflows (Services, Async Pipelines)

- **Selected**: FastAPI (vlatest)
- **Rationale**: FastAPI provides high-performance, async-first API development with automatic OpenAPI docs. It uses Starlette under the hood, offering low latency suitable for <2s task operations.
- **API Protocol**: HTTP/2 over WebSocket (for real-time updates)

## 12. Database Architecture & Schemas (ER Diagram, Indexing)

- **Primary Database**: SQLite
- **Rationale**: SQLite provides file-based, zero-configuration persistence ideal for single-user apps. It supports ACID transactions and is lightweight.

## 13. API Design & Interface Contracts (Endpoints, Payloads, Errors)

- **Protocol**: HTTP/2 over WebSocket (for real-time updates)
- **Why**: FastAPI supports WebSockets for live task list updates. HTTP/2 reduces latency and improves connection efficiency.

## 14. AI/ML Subsystem Architecture

- **AI Required**: `False`
- **Problem Type**: `NONE`
- **Justification**: The task management system involves only CRUD operations (create, read, update, delete) on a simple Task entity with required fields and validation. All requirements can be satisfied using deterministic approaches: regex for input validation, SQL queries for data retrieval/storage, and rule-based logic for ID generation. No AI/ML capabilities are needed to fulfill the functional or non-functional requirements.

## 15. Dataset Strategy & Data Engineering (Pipelines, Validation)

Dataset strategy unspecified or non-ML project.

## 16. UX Design & View State Specifications (4 States per screen)

| View Name | Loading State | Empty State | Error State | Success State |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TaskForm | Displaying task creation form with spinner replacing input fields | No tasks saved; list is empty | Error message 'Title and description are required' displayed above inputs | Task created successfully; new task appears in TaskList |
| TaskList | Loading spinner replaces task list while fetching from backend | No tasks saved; message 'No tasks to display' shown | Error message 'Failed to load tasks. Please try again.' appears at top | List of tasks with Edit and Delete buttons displayed |
| ValidationMessage | Loading spinner replaces validation messages while checking inputs | No errors; message 'Task created' shown after success | Error message 'Title and description are required' shown above fields | Success message 'Task updated' displayed after edit or delete |

## 17. Security Architecture & Threat Model (STRIDE Catalog)

- **Authentication**: No authentication
- **Authorization**: Single-user local access; no application roles

| Threat ID | STRIDE | Severity | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T-001 | Spoofing | HIGH | Potential unauthorized task creation or data corruption. | Validate all incoming payloads on FastAPI server using Pydantic models and reject malformed requests. |
| T-002 | Tampering | MEDIUM | Inconsistent UI state and potential logic bypass. | Enforce schema validation on FastAPI endpoints; reject unsupported field modifications. |
| T-003 | Denial of Service | CRITICAL | Application becomes unresponsive to all users, violating SLA. | Implement per-client connection rate limiting and graceful disconnect handling. |

## 18. Verification & QA Test Pyramid (Test Cases, Load Thresholds)

- **Test Pyramid**: {"unit": "80%", "integration": "15%", "e2e": "5%"}

| TC-003 | Task Deletion API | e2e | Delete task and verify removal from list | API returns 204 No Content; subsequent retrieval shows task absent | REQ-F-001 |

## 19. Complete Technology Stack Table

| Storage | SQLite with WAL mode enabled | latest | WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) ensures crash safety by allowing safe concurrent reads/writes. SQLite is embedded and file-based. |

## 20. Rejected Technology Alternatives & Trade-Offs Matrix

| Technology Category | Selected | Rejected Alternatives & Reasons |
|---|---|---|
| UI Framework | React | Vue.js: Less mature ecosystem for rapid prototyping; not as optimized for TypeScript integration in this context.; Angular: Overkill for simple CRUD operations; adds unnecessary complexity (e.g., RxJS, dependency injection) without benefit. |
| Web Framework | FastAPI | Django REST Framework: Over-engineered; adds unnecessary layers (ORM, serializers) and synchronous defaults that may not meet performance targets.; Flask: Lacks built-in async support and auto-docs; requires manual configuration for high-performance endpoints. |
| Persistent Storage | SQLite | PostgreSQL: Overkill; requires server setup, configuration, and maintenance beyond scope of a local app.; MongoDB: Not relational; unnecessary complexity for simple CRUD on a single entity. |
